title: Use a substitution
text: Let $$u=1\theta.$$ First, find the general solution for the simpler equation $$\cos(u)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$

title: Find the general solution for u
text: On the unit circle, cosine is positive $$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$ at $$\frac{\pi}{6}$$ and $$-\frac{\pi}{6}$$. $$Since$$ $$cosine$$ $$has$$ $$a$$ $$period$$ $$of$$ $$2\pi, $$ the general solution for $$u$$ is $$u=\pm\frac{\pi}{6}+2n\pi.$$

title: Substitute back
text: Now substitute $$2\theta$$ back in for $$u$$ to get $$2\theta=\pm\frac{\pi}{6}+2n\pi.$$

title: Isolate theta
text: To solve for $$\theta$$ divide the entire equation by $$2$$. You must divide the angles AND the period term ( $$2n\pi$$ ).
